clue.text: On top of the world getting the perfect start at Silverstone

definitions.meaning: literally, standing at the North or South Pole, the very top (or bottom) of the globe
the front slot on a Formula One starting grid, earned by the fastest qualifier

explanation.surface: A driver feels elated after securing the ideal grid slot at the British Grand Prix.
explanation.walkthrough: Silverstone is the circuit in Northamptonshire that hosts the British Grand Prix. The first reading takes the phrase literally: a spot at the Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: a polar location literally, and the motor-racing term for the first grid slot.

clue.text: Porky South American's muscle less than frightening

parts.note: a pec is a chest muscle (pectoral)

indicators.note: being less than the word for frightening means it falls just short, losing its first letter

parts.note: frightening means scary

explanation.surface: An unflattering remark about a plump Argentine's physique: his muscles are hardly intimidating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' trims SCARY by its opening S, leaving CARY. 'Porky' is the definition's pun: the animal is pig-like rather than fat.
explanation.definitionFit: The peccary is a wild pig-like mammal of the Americas, so 'porky' describes its kind, not its build.

clue.text: Circuits pass into disuse without Ecclestone's capital

indicators.note: without tells us a letter is taken away from the word for passing into disuse

parts.note: to lapse is to pass into disuse

indicators.note: a capital here is a capital letter, the initial of the name Ecclestone

explanation.surface: Racing circuits fall out of use when Bernie Ecclestone withholds the money.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernie Ecclestone ran Formula One's business for decades; 'capital' pretends to be his money but is just his initial E.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap is one circuit of a racetrack, so the plural matches the plural definition.

clue.text: Heidfeld's finish the prelude to party in press enclosure near 21 across

indicators.note: in puts the two pieces inside the word for press

parts.note: to press things together is to pack them

indicators.note: the prelude to party says that letter comes just before the word for party
a name's finish is its last letter, here of Heidfeld

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Nick Heidfeld's retirement is celebrated with a party in the media area beside the pits.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Heidfeld was a German F1 driver. The 21 across answer is the pit lane, beside which teams work.
explanation.definitionFit: At a racing circuit the paddock is the fenced team area behind the pit lane garages.

clue.text: During the day old Mark in charge of cells

indicators.note: during means these letters sit within the abbreviated day

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, a day
M abbreviates the mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Back in the day, someone called Mark ran the prison cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cells' looks like a prison block but means body cells; 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Somatic means relating to the body, as in somatic cells, the body's non-reproductive cells.

clue.text: Potentially a slick virtuosity replaces content

indicators.note: content is what a phrase contains, so the letters lie inside virtuosity replaces

explanation.surface: A smooth operator's brilliance takes the place of real substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slick' looks like an adjective for a smooth talker; in F1 a slick is a treadless racing tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A slick is one example of the rubber wheel covering, the smooth dry-weather racing type.

clue.text: Australian evergreen melody adapted originally by Electric Light Orchestra making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means the band's initials come back the other way
originally means the band name's first letters are taken

parts.note: an aria is a melody adapted for a solo singer in opera

explanation.surface: A golden oldie reworked by the Electric Light Orchestra for their reunion tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns ELO to OLE; ELO is the 1970s band known by those initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Olearia is a genus of daisy bushes native to Australasia, keeping their leaves all year.

clue.text: Not-so-typical Sunday driver in 'otel in SE13?

parts.note: SE13 is the London postcode district of Lewisham
a Cockney dropping the H turns the hotel chain Hilton into 'ilton, matching the dropped H of 'otel

explanation.surface: Asks whether an unusual weekend motorist might be staying at a hotel in south-east London.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sunday driver is a slow, dawdling motorist; this one races on Sundays, as Grands Prix are held then. SE13 is a London postcode, and 'otel signals the dropped-H accent of Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Formula One champion is a racer whose Sunday driving is anything but leisurely.

clue.text: A number of lefties ignore the sometime bouncer's previous signal that the event is over

definitions.text: signal that the event is over

indicators.note: previous says the bouncer's piece comes before the song

parts.note: a cheque sometimes bounces when the account cannot pay it

indicators.note: ignore the means the song title's article is dropped

parts.note: a number is a song, and the socialist anthem is The Red Flag
the article taken out of the song's title

explanation.surface: Some left-wingers miss an ex-doorman's earlier sign that the party is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Flag is the Labour Party's traditional anthem; 'ignore the' drops its article. 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman but means a cheque that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-white checked banner is waved to mark the end of a motor race.

clue.text: With Massa's rear puncturing, high speed around first corner is missing

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters surround the corner's opening letter and Massa's last
puncturing says Massa's final letter also pierces the jumbled letters
high, as in intoxicated, signals the letters of speed are jumbled
first picks the opening letter of corner
the rear of a name is its final letter

explanation.surface: Felipe Massa suffers a rear-tyre puncture at high speed and misses the first corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' anagrams SPEED to ESPED, 'around' puts C round inside it (ESCPED), and 'puncturing' slips A from Massa in. Massa was a Brazilian F1 driver.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped person or animal has got away and is therefore absent or unaccounted for.

clue.text: Northern town of Grimethorpe cleaned up and regenerated following Morecambe's lead

indicators.note: following says the reworked town name comes after that letter
a word's lead is its opening letter, here of Morecambe
regenerated, like a renewed town, signals the remaining letters are rearranged
cleaned up means the grime is removed from Grimethorpe

explanation.surface: A former mining village is tidied and redeveloped, copying a seaside resort's example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaned up' strips GRIME, leaving THORPE, which 'regenerated' reshuffles to ORPETH. Grimethorpe is a Yorkshire ex-mining village; Morecambe a Lancashire seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Morpeth is a market town in Northumberland, in the north of England.

clue.text: Accidentally maim officer in mosque

indicators.note: accidentally suggests the letters of maim fall into a new order by chance

explanation.surface: Someone inadvertently injures a man at prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The prayer leader of a mosque holds that religious office in Islam.

clue.text: Hammer features in art house horror season's new venue

indicators.note: features in says the knockout joins the letters of art house in one pool to be mixed
horror, in the sense of a mess, signals the letters of art house, with the knockout featured in them, are scrambled

parts.note: to hammer an opponent is to knock him out, KO

explanation.surface: Hammer horror films get shown in an art-house cinema's new season.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammer is the British studio famous for horror films, a decoy here. The Korean Grand Prix was new to the 2010 F1 season.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Asian nation joined the Formula One calendar in 2010, a new racing venue that year.

clue.text: Poor air quality dogs country around Baghdad

indicators.note: to dog is to follow closely, so the quality letter trails the scrambled air
poor means badly formed, so the letters of air are rearranged

parts.note: Q is an abbreviation for quality

explanation.surface: Bad air pollution plagues the region surrounding Baghdad.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital of this Middle Eastern nation, which surrounds it.

clue.text: See 12
Split pistil threatens cultivation

indicators.note: split means the letters run across the split between pistil and threatens

explanation.surface: A broken flower part endangers the growing of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilth is the tilling of land, or soil in its tilled state, so it means cultivation.

clue.text: Rick's familiar greeting can be heard

indicators.note: can be heard says the greeting is spoken, giving a word of like sound

parts.note: hey cock is an informal, matey British greeting

explanation.surface: A man named Rick has a chummy way of saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rick' looks like a name but is a hayrick. 'Cock' is old northern English slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a stack of hay, and a haycock is a small conical heap of it.

clue.text: Amateur north-east champion in command before sharp left-right combination

indicators.note: before puts the champion and command pieces ahead of the rest

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge or in command
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A northern amateur boxing champion lands a quick left-right punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-right combination' suggests boxing but is a road layout.
explanation.definitionFit: On a racing circuit a chicane is a tight S-bend, a quick left then right turn.

clue.text: See 27
Family of chefs not unknown over the water in France for continental roll

indicators.note: over puts the chefs above the water in a down answer
not unknown means the unknown letter is dropped

parts.note: the Roux family are a famous French dynasty of chefs in Britain
X is the mathematician's unknown
French for the water is l'eau

explanation.surface: French chefs across the Channel make a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' sounds like 'famous' but drops X.
explanation.definitionFit: A rouleau is a cylindrical roll, such as a stack of coins wrapped in paper, from French.

clue.text: Knowing about Tina Turner or, like, John, Paul and George — but not Ringo

definitions.text: like, John, Paul and George — but not Ringo

indicators.note: about means the word for knowing goes around the rearranged name

parts.note: knowing in the sense of crafty means sly

indicators.note: Turner, read as something that turns, signals the letters of Tina are reordered

explanation.surface: Tina Turner or the Beatles, excluding their drummer: a pop trivia aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Saints John, Paul and George exist; there is no Saint Ringo, so the definition excludes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints share those three first names but not the drummer's nickname, so 'like them' means holy.

clue.text: Alpine forest's eastern border destroyed to make way for garages

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are broken up and reformed
in an across clue the eastern border of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An Alpine forest's edge is cleared to make room for garages.
explanation.walkthrough: Alpine is also a French car and racing marque, hinting at the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: At a racing circuit the teams' garages line the road from the track used for pit stops.

clue.text: Salsa's athletic stompers suddenly appear beginners in tap dance

indicators.note: dance means the letters jig about into a new order
beginners in means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Energetic salsa dancers suddenly appear as tap-dance novices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salsa' suggests the dance but means a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Passata is sieved tomato sauce, and salsa is Italian and Spanish for sauce.

clue.text: 'I'm forever blowing bubbles' like East Ender reportedly not enamoured of hippie musical

indicators.note: an East Ender, dropping his H sounds, says the phrase aloud

parts.note: someone who dislikes Hair, the 1960s hippie musical, is a hair hater

explanation.surface: A West Ham fan singing the club anthem dislikes the hippie show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm Forever Blowing Bubbles' is West Ham's anthem, sung in London's East End, where Cockneys drop H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that blows air into water forever produces bubbles, like the song's singer.

clue.text: Gloom of seaman out of work

indicators.note: out of means the seaman is taken out

parts.note: labour means work
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's depression when he loses his job.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour is to scowl or look dark and threatening, a verb sense of gloom.

clue.text: Stuck in this, Rosberg's foremost gifts are wasted

indicators.note: wasted, as in ruined, signals the letters are scrambled
foremost picks the opening letter of the driver's surname

parts.note: the opening letter of the German driver's surname

explanation.surface: If he can't change up, Nico Rosberg's talents go to waste.
explanation.walkthrough: Nico Rosberg was a German F1 driver. 'are' is part of the anagram pool, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A car stuck in the lowest ratio crawls along, so a racer's skills are squandered.

clue.text: Count plot as rumour

indicators.note: rumour is hearsay, so the word is given by sound

parts.note: to plot data is to graph it

explanation.surface: A nobleman's scheming is just gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Graf is the German title for an earl or count, a nobleman's rank.

clue.text: See 24
Tail-enders better score in opening session

indicators.note: in puts the score inside the bettor

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a backer
a mark is a score

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of session

explanation.surface: A cricket punter bets on the lower-order batsmen to score in the morning session.
explanation.walkthrough: Tail-enders are cricket's weakest batsmen, a decoy; the answer is the slowest racers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cars at the back of the field are those at the tail end of the race.

clue.text: Open river entering gorge

indicators.note: entering means the river goes inside open

parts.note: overt means open
an ea is a river or stream

explanation.surface: A river opens out as it flows into a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge as a verb is to eat greedily, to stuff yourself.

clue.text: Cutting of magnolia can't have thorny growth

indicators.note: a cutting is a slip taken from a plant, here a stretch cut from the words

explanation.surface: A slip from a magnolia mustn't have spines.
explanation.definitionFit: An acantha is a spine or prickle, a sharp thorn-like outgrowth on a plant or animal.

clue.text: Source of 'I'm going to stop the start watch' and similar slips — nonsensical malarkey with unmistakably rhapsodic race tips in-between

definitions.text: Source of 'I'm going to stop the start watch' and similar slips

indicators.note: nonsensical means the letters are jumbled into nonsense
tips are the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A famous commentator's gaffes are gibberish, though excitedly delivered with racing tips.
explanation.walkthrough: The veteran BBC F1 commentator was famous for gaffes called Murrayisms, including the quoted line.
explanation.definitionFit: The F1 commentator originated many such verbal blunders, so he is their source.
